input.content: You are operating a real coding sandbox. You must solve the task by calling the provided tools. Do not only explain a solution and do not output a code block instead of editing files. Your first action must be a list_files tool call. Then inspect the relevant files, make the smallest correct edit with edit_file or write_file, run_tests, and finally call submit. Ordinary assistant text does not modify the repository and will receive a failing reward.

funcy/colls.py offers where() and its lazy twin iwhere() for picking records out of a list of dicts by keyword condition, for example where(rows, status='open'). They work when every record carries every key that is named in the condition, but real record sets are ragged - some rows simply do not have the field - and then instead of skipping the record that lacks the key, both functions blow up with a KeyError and the caller loses the whole result. A record that does not carry a key named in the condition cannot possibly match it, so it should just be filtered out, and a condition naming a key that no record has should yield an empty result rather than an error. Be careful that a key which is genuinely present but holds None is still different from a key that is absent. Do not change any public signature, do not change which of the two functions is eager and which is lazy, and fix both of them - callers use each.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files in the sandbox, recursively. Start here to see the repo layout.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file with line numbers. Returns at most 200 lines per call; use start/end to page through longer files.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write a whole file, replacing any existing content. Prefer edit_file for small changes.

content.description: The complete new contents of the file.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace one exact snippet in a file. old_str must appear exactly once - include surrounding lines to make it unique.

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description: Run the visible smoke tests. These are a sanity check, not the grading tests - passing them does not mean the task is solved.

tools.name: submit
tools.description: Finish the task. Call this once the fix is in place; the episode ends immediately.
